title: Escalation Triage Grid — adaptive capacity hedging for strategic accounts
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: Strategic customers run into two common failure modes when requesting roadmap commitments: (1) ad-hoc escalations that bypass prioritization and overload delivery lanes, and (2) early-stage escalations where scope/quality trade-offs are unclear and commitments are made without capacity hedges. Both lead to missed expectations and churn.

This ticket scopes a product-led solution — the Escalation Triage Grid (ETG) — to standardize intake, assign dynamic SLA-backed delivery bands, and provide automated hedging recommendations (e.g., scope fractions, canary rollouts, and fallbacks) tied to resource availability and account priority. The ETG will be surfaced in the Console intake flow and the internal PM dashboard so we can operate consistently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers.
background: We currently accept prioritized asks from high-touch accounts via email, CSMs, and ad-hoc meetings. PMs make subjective commitments based on account signals without a formal capacity hedge. Engineering has asked for clearer SLAs and scope bands to reduce last-minute context switches. Design has prototypes for a lightweight intake widget. This work aligns with company thesis: make serving commitments predictable while protecting delivery economics.
proposed_solution:
1) Define a 4x3 triage matrix (Account Gravity: low/medium/high/high+ vs. Impact urgency: Exploratory/Required/Critical) that maps to delivery bands (Info, Monitor, Scoped Delivery, SLA-backed Delivery).
2) For each band, define default SLAs (response window, commitment horizon) and pre-approved hedges (scope fraction, canary %, fallback model variant).
3) Implement ETG intake in Console: dynamic recommendations, required fields (customer ask, rationale, success criteria, rollback triggers).
4) Expose an internal PM dashboard with active escalations, current capacity utilization (via ENG telemetry), and a one-click "apply hedge" that creates scoped PRD + rollout checklist.
5) Link automation to engineering routing so high+critical items can open Dedicated capacity reserve requests or trigger canary policies.
acceptance_criteria:
- ETG decision matrix documented and approved by PM, Eng, and Design.
- Console intake widget prototype in design Figma and validated in 3 discovery sessions with CSMs.
- Backend API spec for intake created and reviewed with ENG.
- PM dashboard shows mocked capacity signals and allows approval/assignment flows.
- Two pilot escalations processed end-to-end with applied hedges and recorded outcomes.
- Runbook created for on-call/triage rotation and SLA enforcement steps.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Design & Spec): finalize matrix and SLAs; design widget and dashboard prototypes. (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Backend & Dashboard MVP): API, persistence, and internal UI with mock telemetry. (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (Console Integration & Pilot): sample customers + internal high-touch accounts; collect feedback and iterate. (3 weeks)
Phase 4 (Launch & Ops): enable full Console flow, update CSM playbooks, train PMs/Eng, set monitoring alerts. (2 weeks)
success_metrics:
- Reduction in ad-hoc unscoped escalations by 60% within first 2 quarters.
- 90% of top-account escalations processed through ETG within SLA windows.
- Fewer than 10% of ETG-scoped deliveries result in rollback-level incidents.
- PM satisfaction score for intake process >= 4.2/5 in post-pilot survey.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Overhead causes PMs/CSMs to avoid using ETG. Mitigation: keep required fields minimal and provide a quick "triage-lite" path for exploratory asks.
- Risk: Engineering capacity signals are noisy. Mitigation: start with conservative capacity thresholds and require manual approval for automatic hedges.
- Risk: Customers interpret SLAs as contractual promises. Mitigation: clearly label initial pilot SLAs as operational guidance and add legal/finance review before committing in contracts.
